About This Job
Senior Care Assistant
Pay starting at £29,000 per annum
We are looking for individuals with a kind, compassionate heart who want to make a true difference to the quality of life for our clients, to join our team.  As a Senior Care Assistant you will be the link between our Care Manager, and the Care Assistant team, you will conduct introductions between clients and Care Assistants, conduct training for the Care Assistant team, and provide a variety of non-medical services to help clients keep independent in their own home. You will be based both within the field, when providing care to our clients, and in the office when supporting the Care Manager.
You will have a passion for supporting others and pride yourself on delivering an outstanding service. You will be reliable, trustworthy and respectful. You will enjoy building professional friendships and comfortable spending time in the company of others.
As a Senior Care Assistant you will also help to ensure that Home Instead Aylesbury Vale and North East Oxfordshire remain CQC compliant, by supporting our Care Manager in this area.
This role is a full-time position, with guaranteed contracted hours. You will therefore be expected to work alternative weekends in addition to a minimum of two evenings per week, as a part of your working availability.

Qualifications
As a Senior Care Assistant you must have achieved or be actively working towards a Level 2 qualification in Health and Social care. Experience within the care sector is essential, you must have a passion for delivering good customer service, and have knowledge and understanding of legislation specific to Health Social care.
A valid drivers license and access to a reliable form of transportation is also required for this role, where you will be providing support to our clients within the communities we serve. You will also be flexible to travel to all geographical areas encompassed within our patch.
You will receive industry leading training, great rates of pay and excellent support.
Benefits Include:
• Guaranteed hours built around your availability
• Optional overtime opportunities
• Competitive rates of pay starting at £29,000 per annum
• Mileage payment of 45p per mile
• Minimum of an hour visit per client
• Travel time between clients with flexibility depending on the distance of travel
• Paid annual leave
• Employee health assured program
• Pension auto-enrollment
• Higher rates of pay for bank holidays
• Staff Benefits including a range of high street stores, holidays, etc.

Additional Information
If you're looking for work which is extremely rewarding, part of the community and you have the willingness to learn, we would love to hear from you. Please click on 'I'm Interested' or alternatively, contact us on 01296 410029  between 9am and 5pm, Monday to Friday.
We encourage applications from all sections of the community as we want to reflect the neighbourhoods in which we work. Home Instead is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of adults and expects all staff to share this commitment.

About This Job
Home Instead Stockport are looking for caring, friendly individuals to help us support people to stay independent in their own home, by visiting them and offering assistance and companionship. We match our Care Professionals and clients together based on skills, personality and interests. Visits with any client who is new to you are always introductions with the support of another colleague, so you can really get to know your clients, and you won't be thrown in at the deep end.
We know you can't provide the highest standard of care during short visits, and no one wants to be rushed. That's why we have minimum 1-hour visits plus suitable travel time to ensure you can take your time with clients, with mileage reimbursement.
We have a range of part-time options available, but you must be able to commit to at least 3 weekdays plus alternate weekends. Popular shift options are 8am - 2pm, 4:15pm - 8:45pm or 5:30pm - 10:15pm. The days you work will always be the same, allowing you to plan ahead.
Benefits:
• £13.00 - £14.00 per hour plus 35p per mile.
• £26 - £28 per hour on bank holidays.
• Paid face-to-face training delivered by a Registered Nurse.
• Paid shadowing calls with your matched clients.
• Access to early pay scheme - be paid up to 50% of your monthly earnings instantly.
• No uniform, stay comfortable in casual dress alongside your free Home Instead satchel, ID badge and PPE.
• Gain qualifications - you will earn your Care Certificate, and have the option to undertake your Level 2 or 3 Diploma, or City & Guilds certificates.
• Refer a Friend Bonus - you and your friend will earn £250 EACH per referral.
• Opportunities for career progression e.g. Care Quality Lead.
• Access to Blue Light Card and Home Instead discounts.
• We pay for your enhanced DBS check.
• Support of local office in Offerton with glowing CQC report and a score of 9.8/10 on homecare.
Responsibilities as a Domiciliary Home Care Assistant:
• Support with household tasks such as tidying, cleaning and laundry.
• Make, or assist to make your client's favourite meals.
• Offer companionship and social support, engaging with your client's hobbies and getting to know what they enjoy most.
• Support with personal care tasks such as getting washed and dressed for the day.
• Take your client out to places of their choice, e.g. to the local shops.
• Write accurate daily notes and report any concerns as per company procedure.
• Administer medication and record appropriately.
Requirements:
• Experience is not required due to our comprehensive in-house training. However, we would love to hear about any previous care experience either professional or personal, if you have this.
• You must have a full driver's licence and your own vehicle.
• You must be reliable and punctual to ensure we can continue to provide an excellent service to our clients.
• Must have a caring, friendly personality.
• Must be able to commit to our hours options and work alternate weekends.
• Must live in or near Stockport.
Sound interesting? Pop your application through, and let's have a chat!
Unfortunately, we do not have a licence to offer sponsorship.
By submitting your application you are accepting our terms contained within our data protection promise. Please contact the office for more information.
Job Type: Part-time

About This Job
We are looking for people with kind, compassionate hearts who want to make a true difference to the quality of life for our clients to join our team in Harrogate, Ripon and Thirsk. As a Live In Care Professional, you will live in the client's home and provide a variety of non-medical services to help them keep independent in their own home.
The role of a Live In Care Professional is both rewarding and enjoyable, working in partnership with the client's family and the Home Instead Team.
• As a Live-In Care Professional, you will be required to provide the highest quality 24-hour care with the appropriate breaks and non- working time included.
• You will be responsible for delivering your client's personalised care plan and health goals, enabling your client to live life to the full in their own home.
• We specialise in  Dementia and Parkinson's care.
• You will manage your Client’s medical condition, meals, hygiene and ensure their safety at all times.
• You will maintain a positive relationship with your client, their family, friends and those supporting their health and wellbeing as well as being trustworthy and compassionate.
You do not need any particular qualifications to become a Live In Care Professional but you must have the right qualities for the role . It would be useful to have some experience of working in a care setting or interacting with older people. This could be personal experience of caring for a family member or voluntary experience. You will have a passion for supporting others and pride yourself on delivering an outstanding service. You will be reliable, trustworthy and respectful. You will enjoy building professional friendships and comfortable in spending time in the company of others.

Qualifications
In order to become a Care Professional, we will provide all the training and support to get you up to speed.  However, we do look for people with the following:
• Great interpersonal and communication skills
• Positive and caring attitude
• Reliability, flexibility and adaptability
• A passion for supporting others
• Genuine interest in becoming part of a caring team

Additional Information
As a Live In Care Professional, you will be provided with 3 meals a day or an allowance from the client, a separate room to stay and access to a TV and WiFi.  In addition, we offer comprehensive training and support from our local office.
If you're looking for work which is extremely rewarding and satisfactory and have a high-degree of  flexibility to meet our clients' needs, we would love to hear from you. Please contact us on 01423 774490
We encourage applications from all sections of the community as we want to reflect the neighbourhoods in which we work. Home Instead is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of adults and expects all staff to share this commitment. This role is subject to DBS enhanced disclosure.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/capitapersonali.description_excerpt:
About This Job
As a Nurse Assessor/Functional Specialist at Capita HAAS (Health Assessment Advisory Service) you’ll use your clinical expertise and analytical skills in a different way - to meet with benefits claimants in person or via video link, write in-depth reports and make important clinical recommendations, all while enjoying a more structured and flexible way of working.
What we offer
• Excellent training and ongoing support – be part of our valued team where wellbeing is prioritised.
• Full or part time hours (minimum 3 days per week).
• Monday to Friday between 8am to 5pm with no weekend or night shifts (occasional 8pm finishes may be required).
• £39,500 starting salary, rising to £40,500 after DWP approval.
• 10% of Salary Bonus scheme (based on quality and performance).
• Hybrid working – home and clinic based (up to 3 days per week).
• Watch this short video to find out more https://capita.wistia.com/medias/2spl0ey4a9
Please note, due to business needs, part-time staff will be required to work on a Friday each week as part of their usual pattern. Also there will be an initial full time (paid) training period of 8 weeks so candidates must be able to commit to that.
Other benefits
• NMC fees paid and full revalidation support.
• 15 weeks’ full maternity, adoption and shared parental pay.
• Company pension, life assurance and Cycle2Work scheme.
• Discounts across retail, travel, technology and wellbeing.
• Free access to Headspace (for you and up to 5 others).
• A paid volunteering day each year.
• Ongoing training, development and clear career pathways.
• 25 days’ holiday (rising to 27 with service) with the option to buy more up to 5 days.
What you’ll do in this role:
• Conduct functional assessments which include initial reviews, face-to-face, video or telephone assessments to evaluate how a claimant’s health condition or disability affects them for various types of benefit.
• Analyse and interpret clinical information and supporting evidence.
• Write detailed evidence-based reports to support the DWP/DfC in making informed and objective decisions - no treatment or diagnosis required.
• Use IT systems to support clinical decision-making and report writing.
• Develop your clinical knowledge and constantly learn about health conditions which are less familiar to you.
What are PIP and WCA?
• Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
• Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

Qualifications
About you
• NMC registered Nurse (RGN, RMN or RNLD)
• Minimum of one year’s post-registration experience.
• Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
• Ability to produce clear, accurate and detailed reports.
• Comfortable working quickly to meet structured targets.
• Good IT skills including Microsoft Office, and the ability to learn new systems while working remotely.
• excellent observational and communication skills, giving you the ability to listen, empathise and dig deeper.
• A driving licence or access to transport for assessment centre working.
Please note: all candidates must hold the right to work in the UK as we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Additional Information
About Capita HAAS
We were awarded two contracts to deliver the Health Assessment Advisory Service (HAAS) assessments in the Midlands and Wales for the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), and in Northern Ireland for the Department for Communities (DfC).
We deliver assessments for a variety of different benefits, including delivering PIP, WCA and Specialist benefit assessments across the Midlands and Wales, and in Northern Ireland.
Security and compliance
Successful candidates will be required to successfully complete government baseline personnel security standard vetting. This is the recognised standard for the pre-employment screening of individuals with access to government asset.
This role is defined as regulated activity relating to children or vulnerable adults within the meaning of the Safeguarding Vulnerable Groups Act 2006 it is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. At vetting, you will undergo an enhanced criminality check which will show both spent and unspent convictions.
What happens next?
Please do complete our short application form and upload your CV. (Please ensure there are no unexplained gaps in your CV).
We’re an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from all backgrounds.
As a Disability Confident Leader, we are proud to guarantee interviews for disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for this role.
If you have queries, or want to discuss any reasonable adjustments, please contact our friendly recruitment team:
Phone - 02035 970410
Email - haasrecruitment@capita.com

About This Job
Help protect the trust behind investing.
At AJ Bell, we believe investing should feel good.
For our customers, that starts with trust. They trust us to look after their investments, operate responsibly and maintain the high standards they would expect from a business handling their financial futures.
Our Financial Crime team plays an important role in protecting that trust.
We’re looking for an experienced Trade Surveillance Analyst to join the team and help protect the integrity of our business, our markets and the interests of our customers.
As a subject matter expert in market abuse, you’ll carry out trade surveillance, investigate potential concerns and use your judgement to identify activity that may require further action.
You’ll also play an important role in continually strengthening our controls, processes and understanding of market abuse risk.
What does the job involve?
You’ll take ownership of trade surveillance activity and investigations, working closely with colleagues across the business and supporting our Financial Crime Manager.
Your responsibilities will include:
• Carrying out daily trade surveillance and investigating alerts to identify potential market abuse.
• Reviewing internal referrals relating to potential market abuse and poor market etiquette.
• Documenting investigations clearly and accurately, including findings, rationale and outcomes.
• Drafting Suspicious Transaction and Order Reports (STORs) for submission to the FCA, where agreed with the Financial Crime Manager.
• Drafting and submitting Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) to the National Crime Agency.
• Supporting responses to regulatory requests for information.
• Identifying opportunities to strengthen our market abuse controls and surveillance processes as regulation and risks evolve.
• Supporting the development and maintenance of market abuse policies and procedures.
• Producing meaningful management information to help identify trends, risks and areas requiring further attention.
• Sharing your expertise across the business, including supporting the development and delivery of training.
• Working with the Financial Crime Manager on the continued development of our approach to trade surveillance and market abuse risk.
What are we looking for?
You’ll already have hands on experience of market abuse surveillance and be comfortable investigating activity, reaching evidence based conclusions and clearly documenting your rationale.
We’re looking for someone who has:
• Previous experience working in market abuse or trade surveillance. This is essential.
• A good understanding of equities, fixed income securities and funds.
• Strong knowledge of the Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) and relevant financial crime and anti-money laundering requirements.
• A good understanding of the behaviours and high-risk indicators that can signal potential market abuse.
• Strong analytical and investigative skills, with the ability to interpret information and make sound judgements.
• Excellent attention to detail, particularly when documenting investigations and regulatory matters.
• The ability to prioritise effectively and work to regulatory and internal deadlines.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills and the confidence to work with stakeholders across the business.

About This Job
Start here. Grow here.
We are constantly evolving to remain at the forefront of innovation, and we're on the lookout for talented, dedicated, and passionate individuals to join us. As a Senior/Principal Project Manager, you will lead multidisciplinary teams to deliver water sector projects from feasibility through to design, construction support and commissioning. We have over 150 people in the Water Team in Scotland, with offices in Glasgow, Edinburgh, Perth and Inverness.
We are delivering a diverse and high-impact portfolio of projects that are shaping sustainable and resilient water systems for generations to come.
We are a Primary Designer on Scottish Water’s SR27 Enterprise. This is a transformational multi-billion-pound programme and will reshape Scotland’s water and wastewater infrastructure from 2027 to 2033 (with potential to extend for another 6 years). Alongside SR27 we are delivering a number of frameworks both direct, and via design and build contractors, to Scottish Water.
Additionally, we have a strong flood and surface water management team providing complex integrated river and coastal modelling, flood prevention and restoration schemes through a number of frameworks, including Excel Scotland.
Responsibilities
• Deliver projects in line with client and AECOM requirements
• Define project scope, schedule, resources and risks
• Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, stakeholders and project teams
• Mentor and develop Project Managers and other team members, promoting collaboration and knowledge sharing
• Manage project commercial performance, including forecasting, costs and cash flow
• Oversee effective contract administration and quality delivery
• Manage subcontractors and suppliers where required
• Contribute to business development through proposals, client engagement and future opportunities
• Champion a positive health, safety and wellbeing culture
About You
• Extensive experience managing projects within consultancy, engineering or infrastructure environments
• Experience in leading bids, proposals or business development activities
• In-depth knowledge of NEC contracts, particularly PSC
• Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary and multi-organisation teams
• Able to balance multiple priorities and work collaboratively
• Proficient in project management and digital collaboration tools
• Water sector experience desirable

Qualifications
Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?
Here’s what we’re looking for:
• Degree in Project Management, Engineering, Environmental Science, Construction Management or a related discipline
• A strong track record of delivering projects successfully
• Knowledge of NEC3/NEC4 contracts advantageous
• APM PMQ, PRINCE2 or equivalent qualification (desirable)
• Chartered or working towards professional membership (APM, PMI, CIOB, ICE, RICS) desirable
• Security clearance checks may be required

Additional Information
We celebrate diversity, including neurodiversity, and believe it enriches our team. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and abilities. If you are an applicant with a disability that requires reasonable accommodation to complete the application process, please contact us at ReasonableAccommodations@aecom.com. At AECOM, we value everyone's unique contributions and perspectives.
Interested in the role or curious about life at AECOM? Follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube to explore our AECOM voices, employee stories, latest projects, and much more!
For further information about the role, reach out to the recruiter on LinkedIn – Laura Easdon.
At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.
About AECOM
AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm and its Professional Services business had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. See how we are delivering sustainable legacies for generations to come at aecom.com and @AECOM.
Freedom to Grow in a World of Opportunity
You will have the flexibility you need to do your best work with hybrid work options. Whether you’re working from an AECOM office, remote location or at a client site, you will be working in a dynamic environment where your integrity, entrepreneurial spirit and pioneering mindset are championed.
You will help us foster a safe and respectful workplace, where we invite everyone to bring their whole selves to work using their unique talents, backgrounds and expertise to create transformational outcomes for our clients.
AECOM provides a wide array of compensation, benefits and well-being programs to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. We’re the world’s trusted global infrastructure firm, and we’re in this together – your growth and success are ours too.
Join us, and you’ll get all the benefits of being a part of a global, publicly traded firm – access to industry-leading technology and thinking and transformational work with big impact and work flexibility. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in each person’s potential, and we’ll help you reach yours.

About This Job
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.
Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!
Thanks for stopping by. We know job descriptions can feel a bit formulaic sometimes, but we promise Canva is anything but. If you're drawn to what we're building and you see yourself in this role, we'd love to hear from you.
Where and How You Can Work The buzzing Canva London campus features several buildings around beautiful leafy Hoxton Square in Shoreditch. While our global headquarters is in Sydney, Australia, London is our HQ for Europe, with all kinds of teams based here, plus event spaces to gather our team and communities. You'll experience a warm welcome from our Vibe team at front of house, amazing home cooked food from our Head Chef and a variety of workspaces to hang out with your team mates or get solo work done. That said, we trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals, so you have choice in where and how you work.
What You'd Be Doing in This Role
Our Account Executives work closely with customers to understand their goals and show them how Canva can help their whole business create and collaborate at scale. As a Mid-Market Account Executive, you'll focus on the DACH region, running a high-velocity, end-to-end sales cycle with a strong focus on new logo attainment.
At the moment, this role is focused on:
• You'll own a targeted book of German-speaking mid-market prospects and run outbound sales activity to identify, engage, and convert new business.
• You'll run a full sales cycle from first outreach to close, using the SPICED methodology to qualify opportunities and uncover real customer value.
• You'll build account plans that are grounded in a data-driven read of the market, translating those plans into targeted, day-to-day sales activity.
• You'll work closely with your manager and senior Account Executives to sharpen your discovery, pitch, and negotiation skills as you build toward more complex deals.
• You'll keep accurate, up-to-date records of pipeline, forecasts, and customer interactions in Salesforce.
• You'll collaborate with Sales & Success, Marketing, and Product to keep the customer experience seamless from first conversation through to close.
• You'll stay close to trends in the DACH mid-market so you can speak credibly to what's changing in your customers' businesses.
You're Probably a Match If:
• You have some experience in outbound sales, ideally in a B2B or SaaS environment, and you're hungry to build a career in mid-market sales.
• You're a confident, clear communicator in both German and English, and you're comfortable presenting to multiple stakeholders.
• You're organised and self-motivated, with the discipline to manage a full pipeline and hit consistent activity and conversion targets.
• You're coachable — you take feedback well and are looking for a team that will invest in developing your sales craft.
• You're familiar with CRM and outreach tools (e.g. Salesforce, Outreach.io, Sales Navigator, Gong), or you're quick to pick up new systems.
About the Team
Our Sales & Success team is part of Canva's Go-To-Market org, on a mission to scale Sales-Led ARR to $100M and help every kind of business empower their teams to design. You'll sit within our High Velocity motion, working alongside AEs focused on SMB and mid-market customers, with dedicated enablement — including quarterly skills priorities like discovery and pitch — to help you grow fast. From whiteboards to docs, to presentations and our AI platform Magic Studio, our Sales team helps businesses create and collaborate at scale.
What's in It for You?
Canva has grown hugely over the last few years, but we're only just getting started. Here's a taste of what's on offer:
• Equity packages — so you share in Canva's success
• Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
• An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
• Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally
Other stuff to know We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture. When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process.

You will provide tailored careers advice and guidance to prisoners through both one-to-one sessions and group workshops. You will create and manage personalised learning plans to help prisoners to identify and work towards their goals during custody and in preparation for release. Your role will support rehabilitation by equipping individuals with the skills, qualifications, and opportunities needed to secure employment or further training upon release.

• Stakeholder management: Engage with prison education departments, training providers, employers and probation services to create employment pathways.
• Quality Recording: Work towards agreed KPIs, targets, ensuring quality assurance standards in accordance with the service provider are met.

• Experience delivering guidance, support or advisory services to individuals

About This Job
The Avaloq Security team is an international team of senior and expert software engineers. The team develops and maintains central application security frameworks, platforms, and tools across company-wide technology stacks and consults business and technology teams on best-practice implementations for context-specific security requirements.
The team operates group-wide application security assessments, monitors and manages security vulnerabilities, and supports business teams in defining and implementing effective risk mitigation measures.
As a Senior Software Engineer in the Security Assurance team, you will play a key role in developing and maintaining the automation, tooling, and CI/CD capabilities that embed security into the software development and release lifecycle. You will work across software engineering, DevOps, cloud, application security, and vulnerability management to build scalable solutions that enable development teams to deliver secure and high-quality software.
Your key tasks
• Design, implement, and maintain internal CI/CD pipelines and automation tooling supporting vulnerability management, security assurance, reporting, and efficient software development workflows.
• Develop and maintain security integrations across the software delivery lifecycle, including source-code, repository, dependency, and container security scanning.
• Develop and maintain backend services and APIs supporting security scanning, vulnerability analysis, event processing, reporting, and integration with internal platforms.
• Monitor and maintain the daily automated build and security validation processes, analyse security warnings and findings, and provide guidance or implement fixes as required.
• Evaluate and validate detected vulnerabilities, assess exploitability and risk, investigate false positives, and support or develop appropriate remediation solutions.
• Maintain and enhance automated security analysis and vulnerability-processing workflows, including event-driven processing and integration with issue-management systems such as Jira.
• Develop and maintain security reporting and dashboards that provide actionable insights into vulnerabilities, remediation status, security risks, and compliance.
• Work with containerized applications and cloud-native environments, including Kubernetes, OpenShift, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI).
• Coordinate security-related actions across multiple teams to ensure the quality, security, and timely remediation of Avaloq products.
• Participate in internal technical discussions, sharing knowledge on secure software development, vulnerabilities, security implementation, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

Qualifications
• University degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, or a related technical discipline.
• Strong experience designing, implementing, and maintaining internal CI/CD pipelines, developer tooling, and automation platforms.
• Senior-level software engineering expertise with hands-on experience in several of the following:
• Java / Spring Boot
• Python
• JavaScript / TypeScript
• Gradle
• Jenkins / Groovy
• REST APIs and service integration
• Event-driven architectures and messaging technologies
• Strong understanding of containerized applications and practical experience with Docker and Kubernetes and/or OpenShift, or similar container orchestration platforms.
• Knowledge and practical experience with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) and cloud-native technologies is highly desirable.
• Deep understanding of application security concepts, security standards, secure software development practices, and industry best practices.
• Practical experience with vulnerability management platforms, security scanning tools, and automated security testing solutions.
• Experience integrating security tooling into CI/CD and software delivery pipelines.
• Understanding of software composition analysis, source-code security scanning, container security, and vulnerability lifecycle management is an advantage.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with excellent attention to detail and a commitment to delivering high-quality, reliable solutions.
• Ability to explain complex technical and security topics clearly to non-technical stakeholders.
• Positive and collaborative mindset, with the ability to work effectively across teams and promote engineering and security best practices throughout the organization.
• Experience or exposure to financial markets and financial products is an advantage.

Additional Information
We realize that managing work life balance is a challenge we all face in our daily lives and in order to support with this we are pleased to offer hybrid and flexible working for most of our Avaloqers to maintain work life balance and still continue our fantastic Avaloq culture in our global offices.

About This Job
We are looking for a motivated and experienced Senior Sustainability Partner to join the Sustainability team at ASOS. This is a delivery-focused, hands-on role responsible for implementing ASOS’s sustainable materials priorities through structured programmes, close and ongoing supplier engagement, strong partnership with Buying and Sourcing teams, and robust data and certification processes.
The role will turn agreed sustainable materials targets and regulatory requirements into clear delivery plans, coordinated supplier actions, effective business processes and measurable outcomes, ensuring solutions are commercially aligned.
The role is a 12-month fixed-term contract reporting into the Head of Sustainability.
What you’ll be doing
Sustainable Materials Transformation
• Lead delivery of annual sustainable materials targets, regularly tracking progress and analysing gaps across fibre, category, supplier and buying area, defining targeted actions at the most relevant level and driving their implementation with suppliers, Sourcing and Buying teams.
• Develop and implement supplier transition plans with priority garment and fabric suppliers, assessing readiness and capacity, agreeing supplier-level actions, providing ongoing support, while ensuring solutions are commercially aligned on cost, quality and speed-to-market.
• Maintain regular, hands-on engagement with key suppliers, driving progress on agreed sustainable materials actions and ensuring delivery against transition milestones and sourcing requirements.
• Map and assess upstream sustainable fibre and material sources across Tier 3 and Tier 4, building insight into availability, capability and commercial terms to identify sourcing opportunities for Buying, Sourcing and Tier 1–2 suppliers.
• Partner with Buying and Sourcing teams to turn sustainable materials goals into practical sourcing solutions, addressing challenges and embedding them into day-to-day product development.
Traceability & Certification
• Lead the tracking, verification and validation of sustainable materials data and certifications at product and fabric level, using certification and chain-of-custody evidence to substantiate sustainable material data across the supply chain.
• Drive the closure of identified gaps through targeted supplier engagement, providing clear guidance on requirements and following up on agreed actions, while coordinating with Sourcing and Fabric teams where wider support is needed.
• Define business needs for certification and traceability data and work with relevant teams to shape the processes and system solutions needed across internal and external platforms, ensuring robust long-term integration.
Compliance, Data & Reporting
• Translate legislative requirements, including ESPR, DPP, ECGT and the CMA Green Claims Code, into readiness plans and embed them into sustainable materials strategy, supplier requirements, processes and tools, in line with the direction and priorities set by the Corporate Affairs and Strategy team.
• Work with technical and data teams to improve systems, dashboards and processes to support sustainable materials reporting and regulatory requirements.
• Coordinate company and industry reporting on sustainable materials, ensuring data is robust and audit-ready, and manage relationships with key organisations such as Textile Exchange, Better Cotton and Canopy.
Team Management & Programme Delivery
• Coordinate delivery across multiple workstreams, track progress, dependencies and risks, and provide clear updates and recommended actions to stakeholders.
• Manage the Sustainable Product Team’s day-to-day delivery, allocating work, setting clear priorities and removing operational blockers.
• Support team performance and development through clear objectives, regular feedback and practical coaching.

• 5+ years’ experience working in sustainability within fashion, apparel or retail, with evidence of delivering programmes from plan through to implementation.
• Strong understanding of sustainable materials, supply-chain traceability and certification standards across polyester, cotton and MMCFs.
• Practical experience working with complex supply chains, including hands-on supplier engagement and progress monitoring.
• Strong commercial awareness, with experience delivering sustainable materials solutions that balance cost, quality and speed-to-market.
• Strong analytical and data-management skills, including the ability to validate supplier, material and certification information and deliver accurate, audit-ready reporting.

• Strong project management skills, with experience coordinating multiple workstreams, milestones, deadlines and dependencies in a fast-paced environment.

As a Business Analyst, you'll work at the intersection of business, engineering, information management and technology, driving the success of complex, large-scale digital transformation projects. Your expertise will ensure the seamless flow of information, alignment of business processes with enterprise digital solutions, and successful adoption of new ways of working.
This is an exciting opportunity to guide stakeholders through digital transition initiatives, helping shape and implement solutions involving Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), Application Lifecycle Management (ALM), Information Management and enterprise platforms such as Dassault Systèmes 3DEXPERIENCE (3DX), Asset Suite 9 and similar enterprise solutions.
Working closely with business leaders, architects, developers and delivery teams, you will ensure that business requirements, information requirements and process improvements translate into sustainable business outcomes.

⚡ Information Requirements Management
• Work with business stakeholders to define Information Requirements, ensuring critical data is available in the right tools at the right time.
• Elicit, analyse, document and manage business, functional and information requirements throughout the project lifecycle.
• Develop and maintain Requirements Catalogues, traceability matrices and business process documentation.
• Identify systems integration needs, reporting requirements, data governance requirements and opportunities for information model development.
• Support the implementation and optimisation of PLM, ALM and Information Management solutions.
⚡ Digital Transition & Change Management
• Support digital transformation initiatives and business change programmes associated with the implementation of enterprise information management systems.

• Support business readiness, adoption and change management activities throughout programme delivery.

• Analyse and document information flows, identifying data quality risks, governance challenges and opportunities for improvement.
• Develop and maintain business process models using BPMN and recognised process modelling techniques.
• Assess end-to-end information flows across engineering, project delivery, asset management and operational functions.
• Support the definition of information architectures, information lifecycles and data management frameworks.
• Identify opportunities to standardise and optimise business processes to improve efficiency and data quality.
⚡ Collaboration and Problem-Solving

• Guide business stakeholders through Information Management, PLM and ALM transformation initiatives.
• Collaborate with Information Architects, Process Architects and Development Teams to deliver integrated digital solutions.
• Facilitate workshops, requirements gathering sessions and stakeholder engagement activities to resolve complex business challenges.

⚡ Project and Workload Management
• Oversee a portfolio of 2–4 projects at a time, ensuring deliverables are completed to agreed quality, schedule and business objectives.

• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives focused on digital adoption, process optimisation and information quality.

⚡ Communication and Reporting

• Promote Information Management, PLM and digital engineering best practice across the organisation.
• Communicate complex technical and process concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

About This Job
Anticipated Contract End Date/Length: May 31, 2027 / 6 months
Work Set-Up: Hybrid
Our client in the global professional services industry is looking for an Executive Recruiter or Search Consultant who will play a key role within their team, combining executive search delivery with rigorous market research, talent intelligence and insight generation. The role partners with business-aligned Leadership Recruiters and Managing Directors to define target markets, identify senior talent and inform leadership hiring decisions across Europe.
The Executive Search Consultant will lead the research workstream across strategic hiring projects, translating business requirements into structured search strategies, market maps and evidence-based talent recommendations for immediate and future leadership needs. This role will focus on European markets within the organisation's well-established team and will act as a subject-matter resource on external leadership talent, competitor activity and relevant market developments.
What you will do
• Position the organisation's Executive Search as a trusted partner by developing close, trusted relationships with Managing Directors and Executive Recruiters.
• Translate search briefs into structured research plans, including target-company universes, sector and functional segmentation, candidate hypotheses, search strings and delivery milestones.
• Conduct confidential, multi-source research and talent identification assignments to identify best-in-class leadership talent for the organisation, using internal and external databases, professional networks, public sources and direct market intelligence.
• Build and maintain detailed market maps, longlists and talent pipelines, ensuring accurate capture of candidate career history, remit, scale, location, mobility and other role-relevant evidence.
• Produce value-adding market and competitor intelligence reports for hiring sponsors, synthesising findings into clear insights on talent availability, competitor structures, talent movement, market constraints and recommended search strategies.
• Identify patterns, gaps and emerging talent pools across searches, and convert them into reusable knowledge, search taxonomies and proactive talent intelligence for future leadership demand.
• Proactively build talent pools of senior executives by directly engaging candidates through multiple channels to articulate the organisation's value proposition.
• Assess candidate suitability against current and future hiring requirements using evidence gathered through research and engagement, aligned with role essentials and the organisation’s leadership profile.
• Discover and evaluate effective, sustainable talent channels and research sources to meet current and future leadership hiring needs.
• Provide a world-class candidate experience to candidates and prospects, acting as an ambassador of the organisation’s talent brand.
• Manage multiple research and search projects in parallel, maintaining clear project trackers, prioritising critical deliverables and meeting agreed deadlines.
• Create clear, executive-ready presentations and written briefings that communicate research methodology, market findings, candidate evidence, risks and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
• Contribute to the continuous improvement of research tools, templates, knowledge management and ways of working across the Leadership Recruitment practice.

Qualifications
• 5+ years of executive search, leadership recruiting, talent intelligence or executive research experience.
• Demonstrable experience delivering executive-level market mapping, talent identification, competitor research and candidate longlisting assignments.
• Prior experience in an executive search firm, in-house executive search function, research-led recruitment environment or relevant talent intelligence role is preferred.
• Strong research capability across databases, professional networks and open-source information, with the judgement to assess source quality and relevance.
• Strong relationship-building skills with senior candidates and internal stakeholders.
• Ability to maintain confidentiality and discretion while working within a large, complex global business.
• Ability to establish trust and act as a credible research and talent adviser to business leaders and recruitment managers.
• Previous experience working with globally distributed teams is preferred.
• Strong understanding of European professional services, technology or digital markets, or the ability to build market expertise quickly through structured research.
Professional Skills Requirements:
• Passion for executive recruitment, research and the ways that evidence-led talent decisions can transform organisations.
• Advanced research skills and the creativity and persistence to uncover hard-to-find senior talent beyond obvious or well-known profiles.
• Strong analytical capability, including the ability to structure ambiguous questions, compare evidence, identify patterns and draw concise, defensible conclusions.
• High attention to detail and commitment to data quality, accurate documentation and consistent research standards.
• Ability to present complex market and candidate information as clear, commercially relevant insight for C-suite and Managing Director audiences.
• Excellent written and oral communication skills at C-suite level.
• Excellent project management skills.
• An inquisitive mindset, intellectual curiosity and a strong external-market orientation.
• Strong organisational and time-management skills.
• Confidence using research platforms, applicant tracking or CRM tools, spreadsheets and presentation software to organise, analyse and communicate findings.

Additional Information

FP&A Manager
Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money.
Min fees. Max ease. Full speed.
Whether people and businesses are sending money to another country, spending abroad, or making and receiving international payments, Wise is on a mission to make their lives easier and save them money.

For everyone, everywhere.
More about our mission and what we offer.

•
You’ll be a trusted finance partner to senior stakeholders, combining financial and operational insight to help them understand performance, key drivers and trade-offs, and make better decisions.
•
You’ll lead planning and forecasting for your areas, challenging assumptions, tracking performance and contributing to longer-term plans.

You’ll build scalable models and reporting for the areas you support, using relevant metrics and scenarios to make risks and opportunities clear.
•
You’ll assess investments, pricing, growth and efficiency initiatives through robust business cases, ROI and payback analysis, providing recommendations that help stakeholders prioritise resources.
•
You’ll lead workstreams within complex cross-functional projects and improve FP&A processes, data quality and reporting in the areas you support, sharing best practice across Finance.

•
Make a visible impact by helping Wise grow sustainably and supporting decisions that advance our mission of lowering prices for customers.
•
Own your own path to success, with the autonomy to make decisions, tackle varied problems and improve how we work.
•
Learn and grow. There’s a lot to be done, and you’ll work on varied challenges across Finance and the wider business.

You’re excited by Wise’s mission and motivated by the role Finance can play in delivering it.

You have proven experience in FP&A, commercial finance, strategic finance or finance business partnering, ideally in a complex or fast-growing organisation.

You have owned planning, forecasting, performance analysis or management reporting processes and understand how the P&L, cash flow and operational drivers connect.
•
You have hands-on experience building structured financial models, working with large or imperfect datasets and using scenarios and sensitivities to support decisions.

You have partnered with senior non-finance stakeholders, challenged assumptions and turned analysis into clear recommendations, becoming a trusted advisor.

You’re analytical and structured, enjoy digging into data and can cut through complexity to identify what matters.

•
You’re humble, curious and comfortable with ambiguity, while willing to challenge assumptions and be direct when needed.

Experience reviewing the work of analysts or mentoring colleagues, whether or not you have formally managed a team.

About This Job
Our clients ask us to make sense of complex, ambiguous problem spaces across digital transformation initiatives, spanning products, platforms, operating models, and data. As a Senior BA here, you’re a problem framer and synthesiser, not an order taker, who turns research, stakeholder input, and data into clear options, a recommendation, and a practical path to value. You partner closely with Product, Delivery, Engineering and Design to shape the “why/what”, enable the “how”, and de-risk delivery end to end.
As a Senior Business Analyst you will deliver for clients today and lean in to building the BA capability here, growing their careers alongside the function as TDG grows.

Qualifications
Who you are:
• A consulting calibre BA: who thrives in ambiguity and brings structured, hypothesis driven thinking to messy problems. You’re not a ticket writer; you create clarity, choices, and decisions.
• Industry relevance: Experienced working to the GOV.UK Service Standard or within the public sector.
• Strategic + analytical: you’re comfortable stepping into ambiguous problem spaces and connecting them to tangible, measurable business outcomes. You help clients break these down into clear, step‑by‑step deliverables, bringing analytical rigour so the work can be planned and delivered with confidence.
• Translational: you turn analysis into meaningful insights that underpin decision making. You work with Product and clients to prioritise benefits and trade‑offs across options and outline practical routes to value. Slides and docs are vehicles for judgement, not the job.
• Stakeholder partner: you build credibility and trust quickly, operating as a trusted advisor and collaborator. You tailor engagement to context and seniority, and you use concise, outcome-led interactions to help stakeholders align and make decisions at pace.
• Delivery pragmatic: you’ve worked effectively in Agile environments, but you can flex your approach to context. You stay focused on client needs and protect outcomes throughout the delivery lifecycle, regardless of framework.
• Digital transformation experience: you’ve led analysis and direction‑setting on complex digital programmes, working across the transformation lifecycle - from early problem framing and research, through analysis and stakeholder alignment, into shaping solution direction and supporting delivery end‑to‑end.
• Mindset: you’re outcomes-focused, commercially aware, and comfortable working in the open - sharing your thinking early and being transparent about potential pitfalls. You bring no ego: you listen carefully, seek feedback early, and adapt your approach based on what you hear.
How you operate:
• Frame the problem & focus areas: Rapidly clarify the problem situation, define hypotheses, and identify the few levers that matter. Stay outcomes‑oriented - keep the bigger picture visible and regularly check scope and decisions against it as delivery progresses.
• Shape options into solution & decision: Build robust options analyses tied to strategy, using clear criteria and stated assumptions. Compare benefits, costs, risks, dependencies, and constraints, and produce decision-ready recommendations.
• Build trust with clients: Create a dynamic that quickly builds strong client relationships by delivering high quality work, actively listening to concerns, and picking up on and responding to feedback.
• Influence decisions through narrative and facilitation: Set the right forums, run crisp workshops, and use compelling narrative to secure decisions - pitch proposals, don’t just present information.
• Stay end-to-end & protect value: Maintain continuity from discovery through delivery: refine scope, ensure deliverables serve outcomes (not the other way around), actively manage risks/assumptions, keep documentation lean and useful, and adapt approach to keep the intended outcomes and benefits intact.
• Measure what matters: Help teams clarify expected benefits, agree what “success” looks like, and support the handover to BAU to ensure the change is embedded and outcomes can be demonstrated.

Additional Information

• Flexible/remote working, Version 1 is tremendously understanding of life events and people’s individual circumstances and offer flexibility to help achieve a healthy work life balance
• Financial Wellbeing initiatives including; Version 1 Pension with a 5% employee-matched contribution, Private Healthcare Cover, Life Assurance, Financial advice and an Employee Discount scheme
• Employee Wellbeing schemes including Gym Discounts, Bike to Work, Fitness classes, Mindfulness Workshops, Employee Assistance Programme and much more.
• 24 days holiday allowance plus Public Holidays, enhanced maternity/paternity leave, marriage/civil partnership leave and special leave policies
• Educational assistance, incentivised certifications, and accreditations, including AWS, Microsoft, Oracle, and Red Hat

We are looking to grow our brilliant team of Care Professionals for morning calls from 07.45 until 12.45.  We provide quality care that makes a real difference to the people we care for at home.  With a minimum of an hour long calls and personalised support with clients who you're matched with, this is home care at its very best.
Our Care Professionals are trained to help our clients remain independent, active and safe.  Every call is different as it's based on the needs of each individual.
As a Home Instead Care Professional, your client visits may consist of:
• Providing personal care.
• Help with medications.
• Preparing meals.
• Light housekeeping.
• Running errands such as accompanying your client to appointments or visiting the shops.
• Helping your client get ready in the morning.
• Offering companionship and conversation.
• Ensuring your client is safe and healthy in their home.
This role is UK-based and the right to work in the UK will need to be established as part of the recruitment process.

Qualifications
No qualifications required.  Full training is provided.  All we ask is that you have a big heart and want to make a difference to our clients lives.

Additional Information
As a Care Professional you will receive industry leading training, great rates of pay and excellent support. Working from 7.45am - 12.45pm and working every other weekend.
Benefits include:
• Regular hours and clients
• FREE DBS
• FREE Care Certificate Training
• Introductions/Shadows to all clients
• Enhanced rate of pay at weekends and bank holidays
• Mileage allowance 40p per Mile
• £500 Refer a friend scheme
• Health Care benefits
• Excellent pension scheme
• No 15-minute call company
• Pay Rates - £13.25 per hour
Due to the nature of the role, caring for clients in their own homes and assisting clients to access the community, we require all of our Care Professionals to have a suitable independent means of transport.
We encourage applications from all sections of the community as we want to reflect the neighbourhoods in which we work. Home Instead  is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of adults and expects all staff to share this commitment. This role is subject to DBS enhanced disclosure.

About This Job
About the role:
Wise protects millions of customers and billions in transactions from fraud, money laundering and financial crime. Our ML systems are the front line of defense - operating at a global scale of 100K requests/minute under strict sub-50ms latency SLAs. We need an exceptional technical leader to own how these models are engineered, shipped and scaled.
We're hiring a Senior ML Engineering Lead to build and grow Wise's Risk Modelling engineering pillar. You will own the full model lifecycle standard for financial crime detection - from offline experimentation to production deployment and real-time monitoring and build the team to execute it. Your job is to build the automated engineering ecosystem and organisation that scales this safely to hundreds of models.
This is a rare greenfield leadership role with strong investment and engagement from Wise's CTO and senior leadership.
How we work:
Risk ML sits within Wise's FinCrime organisation, owning the full ML and AI foundation for financial crime detection. We're have three dedicated pillars - Feature Platform, Learning Loop and Risk Modelling. You'll lead the Risk Modelling pillar, leading a team of Senior ML Systems Engineers and Applied ML Engineers.
We operate with high autonomy and low hierarchy. You'll own the engineering strategy end-to-end - from architecture decisions and infrastructure design through to hiring, team culture and cross-platform partnerships. We value leaders who shape direction and build teams, not just manage delivery.
What will you be working on?:
The Model Factory: Architect the declarative pipeline that turns a configuration file into a deployed, monitored model - the engineering backbone for scaling to hundreds of models
The Experimentation Engine: Establish the reusable path from research (partnering with DS Research) to high-throughput production for traditional and modern architectures
Model Operations: Build the infrastructure for automated retraining, drift detection, threshold simulation/management and audit trails - the operational layer required to run hundreds of models safely at scale
The Team: Recruit, lead and mentor a world-class team of ML engineers. Establish a high-performance, engineering-first culture from scratch - setting hiring standards, technical bar and growth paths
Cross-Platform Partnership: Define and navigate the partnership with key platform teams - owning the build vs consume decisions for your pillar
What do you need?:
You've explicitly led or built an ML Engineering or model lifecycle automation team (not just used one) at a high-growth company - you defined the standards that other engineering teams followed
System-level and mathematical depth: you can design a model factory architecture, review a training pipeline & debug a runtime inference latency regression
Experience in high-throughput environments where latency constraints are tight and model failures carry massive financial consequences
Track record of hiring and developing senior engineers - you've built a team, not just inherited one
Ability to navigate ambiguity and make architecture-level decisions with incomplete information - this is a greenfield build, not an optimisation role
Strong enough technically to guide and review across deep learning, ML systems and production infrastructure - you lead through depth, not just delegation
Nice to Have:
Experience at a tier-1 fintech or payments company
Experience with graph-based methods (GNNs, entity resolution) in production
Foundation model fine-tuning or LLM evaluation experience
Experience establishing ML engineering practices in organisations transitioning from classical ML to deep learning

About This Job
Summary of the Role
The Risk Manager will identify, analyse and respond to risks that arise over the life cycle of a Client programme to help ensure the programme remains on track and meets its goal whilst engaging with stakeholders including other Risk Managers regularly.
Infrastructure project delivery is a challenging environment, with interdependencies between a number of programmes and projects against the need to maintain the military outputs of an operational naval base. The candidate will be required to deliver at pace and demonstrate effective application of programme and project management skills, tools and techniques.
Key Responsibilities
• 🎯 Lead and maintain the Tranche 4 (NBCC Euston) risk register, ensuring risks are accurately identified, assessed and managed.
• 🤝 Collaborate with Joint Programme Team (JPT) risk leads to support the development of the wider programme risk profile.
• 📊 Chair monthly risk review meetings, facilitate risk workshops, produce meeting minutes and deliver monthly risk dashboards.
• 🔍 Identify and manage risks and opportunities, supporting the development and implementation of effective mitigation plans.
• ✅ Conduct regular reviews of risks to eliminate duplication, ensure quality and maintain a manageable risk portfolio.
• 📈 Monitor and report on mitigation actions, tracking progress and ensuring risks are reducing over time.
• 📉 Support Quantitative Risk Analysis activities, including Schedule Risk Analysis (SRA) and Cost Risk Analysis (CRA), and report on modelling outputs.
• 📝 Lead assumptions management and maintain the Master Data and Assumptions List (MDAL).
• 🗺️ Provide strategic risk insights and risk profiling across programme activities and timelines.
• 🌟 Build strong stakeholder relationships, promoting collaboration, trust and effective risk management practices.
• 🤝 Manage relationships with industry partners and suppliers, monitoring performance and addressing emerging issues.
• ⚙️ Ensure compliance with project processes, governance requirements and key infrastructure

Qualifications
Experience & Qualifications
✅ Essential Experience
• 🎯 Minimum 3-5 years' experience in Risk Management, including experience as a Lead or Sole Risk Manager.
• 📍 Available to work on-site 2-4 days per week, depending on business requirements.
• ⚠️ Strong knowledge of risk management processes, frameworks and governance.
• 🔍 Ability to analyse complex data and information to develop a strategic view of risk exposure.
• 📈 Experience identifying trends and providing meaningful risk insights and reporting.
• 👥 Strong organisational, leadership and stakeholder management skills.
• 🏗️ Experience delivering risk management within major infrastructure projects/programmes.
• 🤝 Proven ability to manage delivery teams and engage effectively with a wide range of stakeholders.
• 💻 Strong IT and reporting skills.
⭐ Desirable Experience
• 🌍 In-depth understanding of the infrastructure, construction or government project environment.
• 🗣️ Ability to communicate and influence effectively at senior and executive level.
• 🔄 Adaptable and able to respond quickly to changing business priorities and project risks.
• 🚧 Experience managing risk within complex, live operational environments.
• 🤝 Experience working within collaborative, multi-disciplinary programme teams.
Qualifications & Professional Memberships
🎓 Desirable Qualifications
• APM Project Management Qualification (PMQ)
• PRINCE2 Practitioner
• Managing Successful Programmes (MSP) Practitioner
• Management of Risk (MoR)
• PMI Project Management Professional (PMP)
• Membership of a relevant professional body

This role is primarily based in Helensburgh and due to the nature of the role will have access to restricted information which will require a sole UK National Citizen with SC clearance to meet the necessary security criteria.
There is a requirement to be on the client site to facilitate workshops, routine meetings and site visits and to engage with the wider NBCC team. This currently is a minimum of 2 days per week but could require more at specific times of the programme and should be flexible to facilitate this.
There will be a requirement to attend meetings and workshops in Glasgow, potentially occasional travel to Abbey Wood in Bristol and external offices of contractors if necessary.
Umbrella contractor role.

About This Job
We are seeking an experienced Design Automation Engineer to drive innovation and efficiency across our engineering design processes. In this role, you will leverage technology to automate, streamline, and enhance engineering workflows, helping to improve productivity while maintaining the highest standards of product quality, compliance, and performance.
Working closely with the Senior Application Engineer and cross-functional teams, you will design, develop, implement, and support engineering automation solutions, applications, databases, and integrations. You will play a key role in developing configurable design systems, improving CAD automation capabilities, and ensuring engineering tools support business growth and operational excellence.
This is an exciting opportunity for a technically strong software professional who is passionate about automation, problem-solving, and continuous improvement within an engineering environment.
Key Responsibilities:
• Design, develop, and maintain engineering automation applications using Rulestream, C#.NET, and VB.NET to drive and automate configurable standard designs within Solid Edge.
• Collaborate with the Senior Application Engineer to develop applications, user interfaces, database structures, and system integrations.
• Develop and support engineering design automation solutions that improve efficiency, accuracy, and consistency across design processes.
• Work with SQL Server and Oracle databases to support application development and integration requirements.
• Perform full-stack development across desktop, web, and client-side applications while also acting as a Rulestream Architect.
• Apply industry-standard software design patterns, including Singleton, Factory, MVVM, and MVC, to create scalable and maintainable solutions.
• Support the development and implementation of CAD modelling and drafting standards.
• Partner with engineering, drafting, and operations teams to incorporate Design for Manufacture (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) principles into models and drawings.
• Continuously enhance design automation tools to improve engineering productivity and design accuracy.
• Maintain and support engineering-related tools and outputs, including spreadsheets, calculations, parts lists, and BOM generation processes.
• Develop and maintain system procedures to ensure consistent quality and adherence to company and industry standards.
• Provide technical guidance and training to colleagues and stakeholders where required.
• Produce and maintain technical documentation, user guides, and process documentation.
• Support additional projects and continuous improvement initiatives as required.

Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline.
• Extensive experience in software development.
• Strong experience in CAD Automation and/or Engineering Application Development.
• Experience working as a full-stack developer across desktop, web, and client applications.
• Strong understanding of:
• Rulestream Architect, Engineer, VIA Web and Integration
• ASP.NET, C#.NET, Entity Framework 6, LINQ
• REST and SOAP APIs
• Serialization technologies
• jQuery, AJAX, ReactJS and/or Angular
• Bootstrap and Material UI
• JSON and XML
• WinForms and WPF
• Experience working with SQL Server and Oracle databases.
• Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
• High attention to detail and commitment to delivering quality solutions.
• Ability to communicate effectively in spoken and written English.

About This Job
What will you be doing?
We’re seeking a passionate and experienced Data Analytics Engineer to join a thriving team and help in the design, build and maintenance of scalable data solutions, that bring together data from across the organisation.
You’ll ensure data is well structured, reliable and easy to use for reporting, analytics and in decision‑making. Working as part of the Data Platform Team, you’ll help create a high‑quality, future‑ready data environment that supports business needs now and we continue to grow!
This is a permanent opportunity to be based at our Southampton office with office attendance expected to be 2 days per week.
As a Data Analytics Engineer your responsibilities will include among others,
• Architect and maintain scalable ETL/ELT pipelines, optimising for performance, reliability, cost, and data quality across multiple data sources
• Maintain and troubleshoot medallion architecture and dimensional modelling (star schemas) to support enterprise reporting, KPIs, and Power BI semantic models
• Design, implement, and maintain Lakehouse and Warehouse structures in Microsoft Fabric, including data modelling standards and semantic layers
• Provide operational support, monitoring, troubleshooting, and performance tuning for Microsoft Fabric ingestion, dataflows, and transformation workloads
• Identify, resolve, and prevent data quality issues through validation rules, monitoring, alerting, and root‑cause analysis with source system owners
• Design, build, and maintain enterprise‑standard Power BI reports and dashboards, aligned to agreed data models, governance, and reporting standards

Qualifications
Skills and Experience
To be successful in this role, you should have,
• Demonstrable experience leading the end-to-end delivery of data and analytics initiatives, ensuring outcomes are aligned to both data strategy and broader business objectives
• Ability to own and drive key data projects from concept to production, balancing delivery pace with quality, scalability and measurable business impact
• Experience in partnering with senior stakeholders to shape priorities, translate business strategy into data solutions and ensure delivered products enable effective decision-making
• Strong experience in designing and delivering data solutions on Microsoft Fabric (Lakehouse, Warehouse, semantic models, Power BI), with a strong focus on scalable architecture and data modelling principles
• Advanced SQL and Python/PySpark, applied across ETL/ELT development, optimisation, and automation of data pipelines
• Strong engineering practices experience including performance tuning, platform monitoring and CI/CD with version control (GitHub) within modern data workflows
Desired
• Experience working in Agile / Scrum delivery environments
• Strong collaboration/documentation skills for working with BI developers, analysts, and business stakeholders
• Define and maintain master data structures to deliver a single, accurate client view and ensure consistent data flow across applications
• Some knowledge of Web APIs and deep understanding Spark and SQL Server internals

Additional Information
As a colleague here at S&W you will have access to benefits that include
• Competitive salary
• Private medical insurance
• Life assurance
• Pension contribution
• Hybrid working model (role dependent)
• Generous holiday package
• Option to purchase additional holiday
• Shared parental leave
• Cycle to work scheme
• Season ticket loan
• Eye care support
We are proud to value the differences that a diverse workforce brings, representative of society and our clients. At S&W we have a wide range of highly active employee resource groups and we’re delivering multiple diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives across the organisation. It is our commitment to provide a workplace where all colleagues, regardless of identity, background, or circumstance, feel respected as individuals and feel that they can achieve their full potential and work in a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment.

The role of a Care Professional is to achieve the highest quality of life for the older members of our community. This means providing basic care but also encouraging activities to keep people active, engaged, and confident.

• £200 welcome onboarding payment for training
• Competitive rates of pay £11.10 - £15.80 per hour.

• You will have a passion for supporting others and pride yourself on finding creative ways to improve a person's life.

💕An opening has arisen for the role of Recruiter. At Home Instead, the Recruiter holds responsibility for the end to end recruitment process, from 1) managing the campaigns which generate applicants through 2) screening, 3) interviews, 4) inviting to induction training, 5) the building of the employee digital file, and 6) wellbeing checks until each new hire is several weeks in the role. We are looking for someone who has a passion for people and a natural flair for identifying talent, to select and build a pipeline of high quality, engaged Care Professionals. The type of care we provide is different to most home care services in Northern Ireland (minimum one-hour visits, clients matching with Care Professionals, always introduced, and a variety of care services provided including home help, errands in the community, dementia support, meal preparation and personal care). Candidates respond well to a warm and professional initial contact, including story-sharing which highlights what a typical day looks like as a Home Instead Care Professionals.
Experience of the end to end recruitment process is an advantage, but we recognise that some candidate may have some specialty experience, and may bring other skills alongside such as social media marketing, training, community events, etc.
You will work within the People Team to support our valued Care Professionals through their journey and career with an award winning care business💕You will carry some individual objectives and some team-based KPIs.

·         Manage all aspects of recruitment activity ensuring compliance with legislation, regulators and Franchise Standards.
·         Develop and implement creative recruitment campaigns online and within the local community.
·         Manage the candidate experience creating a positive and engaging proposition.
·         Proactively source candidates using a variety of sources which produce high quality candidates.
·         Develop own networks for sourcing candidates within the local community.
·         Develop and maintain our approach to recruiting on social media by generating interesting, innovative and timely content and campaigns.
·         Research, plan and successfully deliver regular community events including attending fairs, exhibitions, recruitment events and any other appropriate events.
·         Support candidate selection activities.
·         Maintain the accuracy and integrity of recruitment related information using the SmartRecruiters Applicant Tracking System (ATS).
·         Achieve targeted recruitment figures.
·         Ensure compliance with Home Instead’s Equality, Diversity and Equal Opportunities policy, in respect of employment and service delivery.
·         Carry out any other duties deemed necessary for the successful operation of the business.

Qualifications
Essential Criteria
·         Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build rapport quickly.
·         Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
·         Excellent organisation and prioritisation skills with the ability to work accurately under pressure.
·         Team player who is self-motivated, results driven and resilient.
·         Be confident and self-motivated with the ability to build and maintain strong positive relationships
·         Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook with experience using internet sourcing with the ability to learn and adopt new technologies where appropriate.
Desirable Criteria
Previous experience of delivering a responsive end to end recruitment service in a fast paced environment.
Experience of recruitment marketing, social media and other digital communication tools, using a variety of attraction methods to source high quality candidates.
Good understanding of legislation relating to recruitment including Enhanced Criminal Record checks (Access NI), referencing and Right to Work checks.

• Conduct functional assessments which include initial reviews, face-to-face, video or telephone assessments to evaluate how a claimant’s health condition or disability affects them for various types of benefit.

• Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
• Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

• NMC registered Nurse (RGN, RMN or RNLD) or HCPC registered paramedic, occupational therapist or physiotherapist with a valid PIN and no current restrictions

• Good IT skills including Microsoft Office, and the ability to learn new systems while working remotely.
• excellent observational and communication skills, giving you the ability to listen, empathise and dig deeper.

Build the cloud platform that’s transforming electronics design. Altium 365 for cloud lets design engineers communicate, collaborate and bring their ideas to market more efficiently than any platform in the industry.

• Ensure vulnerabilities, once fixed, are permanently prevented from recurring
• Integrate security regression into CI/CD pipelines
• Define coverage targets for security-critical areas (auth, access control, APIs, data flows)

• Lead structured threat modeling sessions for:
• Existing system components
• New features and architectural changes
• Identify attack surfaces, abuse cases, and trust boundaries
• Translate threats into:
• Test cases
• Security requirements
• Mitigation plans
• Ensure threat modeling becomes a continuous lifecycle activity
