We think fast, go big, and always demand more of ourselves. We work hard, deliver, and repeat. We grow with real determination and put success well within reach. We push each other to be better and expect to be pushed back, in a community built on respect, where everyone is counted.
Work Protected.
Overview
This role owns the technical relationship and presales enablement for Mimecast's National Channel Partners. You'll provide technical guidance, training, and hands-on support that helps partners evangelize Mimecast and win deals on their own. This isn't a role where you carry a single deal to close; it's a role where you multiply Mimecast's technical reach across an entire partner community through certification, enablement, and trusted relationships at every level.
You'll work closely with the UK Channel Team, Customer Experience, Service Delivery/Support, Professional Services, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing to keep partners technically sharp and aligned to Mimecast's go-to-market motion.
What You'll Do
• Own the technical relationship with national partner-based Reseller Partners and Managed Service Providers
• Drive and roll out the Mimecast certification program across the National Channel Partner community
• Deliver the partner technical enablement program, including presales training on new releases and go-to-market initiatives
• Present at Mimecast Partner Connect events and run regular update webinars to keep partners informed and upskilled
• Run joint partner and customer demos that bring the full Mimecast platform story to life
• Develop and maintain executive- and manager-level relationships with National Partner leadership
• Enable partners to identify and qualify better-fit opportunities to grow their Mimecast base revenue
• Maintain and grow the partner technical community, tracking and measuring partner engagement over time
• Participate in and lead initiatives that improve Mimecast's positioning in the market with partners, customers, and analysts
• Work closely with internal content creation teams to keep partner-facing technical material current and high-quality
What You'll Bring
Channel relationships are your specialty. You have a demonstrated track record of building and managing technical relationships with resellers, MSPs, or vendors, and you know how to keep a partner community engaged over the long run.
Enablement and training experience matter. You've delivered presales enablement or technical training to channel partners or vendors, and you know how to turn a product release into content a partner's own team can sell and demo confidently.
Indirect sales instincts set you apart. You've worked in a sales environment, especially indirect/channel sales, and you bring real commercial and business acumen to how you prioritize partner time and investment.
Technical depth grounds every conversation. You have hands-on knowledge across Mimecast's Human Risk Management platform: email security, insider risk and data loss prevention, security awareness training, brand and domain protection, and AI-powered threat intelligence, along with the environments partners deploy it into, including Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, identity and directory services, and collaboration platforms like Slack and Teams. You can present technical concepts confidently, tailored to whoever is in the room.
Requirements
• Demonstrated track record of managing technical relationships
• Presales enablement or training experience with Channel partners or vendors
• Experience working in a sales environment, especially indirect sales
• Ability to present technical concepts in a confident and articulate manner tailored to the audience
• Superior analytical and problem-solving skills
• Working knowledge of email security, insider risk/DLP, security awareness training, and brand/domain protection, along with experience with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace
• Working knowledge of corporate and enterprise IT infrastructure, including Active Directory, DNS, networking, TCP/IP, VDI, Citrix, Terminal Services, and application virtualization
• Strong team player who can work cross-functionally across Channel, Customer Experience, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing
Nice to Have
• Familiarity with adjacent security infrastructure such as Crowdstrike, Netskope, or Palo Alto mail/gateway solutions, EPP, SIEM, or DLP
• Familiarity with AI tools (e.g., Claude) to aid in day-to-day enablement and content development
• Relevant industry certifications (vendor-specific, CompTIA Security+, CISSP, or equivalent)
What We Offer
• Hybrid working: balance between office and home that works for you and the team
• The chance to be the technical face of Mimecast within a leading National Partner community
• Room to grow your career in a company that values technical people who can also build partnerships
• The chance to work across a broad and growing platform: email security, insider risk, awareness training, archiving, and more, not just one narrow niche
• Opportunities to represent Mimecast at partner and industry events, webinars, and speaking engagements; we actively support building thought leadership and public profile

Job Title
Senior Electronics Design Engineer, Laboratory Instruments
Location(s)
High Wycombe
Job Description
About the role
Hands-on senior designer in a mission-driven electronics team developing the next generation of material-characterisation laboratory instruments and sustaining the existing product range. You will own subsystems from requirements to verified hardware: low-noise detection front-ends, power distribution, MCU- and FPGA-based control boards, and the integration of cables, actuators and motors. You bring the two things the team needs most: a structured product-design approach and high-speed digital / Xilinx FPGA capability.
What you will do
• Design and verify circuits for the new instrument: low-noise analogue front-ends, mixed-signal, power and control boards.
• Own high-speed digital and FPGA/SoC (Xilinx Zynq) design, and PCB design in Altium 365 to IPC standards.
• Take technical ownership of the electronics architecture for your subsystems, from early concept through prototype, verification and product release.
• Run the product-design process for your subsystems: hardware and product requirements (HRS/PRS), design proposals, design reviews, DFMEA, verification plans and reports.
• Prototype quickly — breadboards, proto and rework boards — to validate concepts ahead of full PCBA spins.
• Bring up, debug and validate boards on the bench with the firmware team; solder, modify and test hardware yourself.
• Own the electrical BOM, component datasheets and the related safety/EMC considerations; support DFM/DFA as designs move from prototype to production.
• Sustain released products: obsolescence and alternates, manufacturing and field issues, root cause.
• Work with optics, mechanics, firmware, software and scientists to prove out designs; coordinate cross-functional issue resolution.
Essential
• Degree in electrical/electronic engineering or a closely related discipline; 5+ years of design engineering in instrumentation or test & measurement products.
• Mixed-signal design in a low-noise environments.
• Digital hardware: MCU-based control boards and communication interfaces — 1G/10GEthernet, USB, SPI, I²C, UART/RS-232, RS-485, CAN, PCIe.
• High-speed multilayer (8+ layer) digital design from schematic to PCB, including DDR3/DDR4 memory interfaces; FPGA/SoC design on Xilinx Zynq in VHDL or Verilog.
• Schematic and PCB design in Altium 365 to IPC-2221 / IPC-7351 with managed-library and version-control discipline; design for manufacture and assembly with a contract manufacturer, including DFM checks (e.g. Valor NPI) and Gerber review (e.g. ViewMate).
• Hands-on PCBA bring-up, test and troubleshooting with digital oscilloscopes, DVMs, spectrum, and logic analysers; test rigs and test plans; disciplined root-cause analysis. Not afraid of practical work — tinkering with circuits and debugging on your own initiative.
• EMC and product safety for laboratory equipment: IEC 61326-1 and IEC 61010-1, through to passing compliance testing.
• Structured product-design approach: requirements, design reviews, DFMEA, verification plans and reports.
• Obsolescence management and sustaining of released products.
• System-integration mindset: how a board fits the rest of the system — cabling, connectivity, harnessing, system diagrams — not only what it does.
Desirable
• Experience with power supply design.
• Working with suppliers and manufacturers: quotes, cost comparisons, assembly options.
• Familiarity with PLM and task-tracking tools.
• Git and Git-based workflows; lean product development with Jira and Confluence.
• Applied use of AI tools and agentic workflows in engineering work
• UV instruments and high-voltage lamp drivers; thermal control and thermal-equipment design.
How we work
• Analytical and data-driven, with attention to detail; sees both the small and the big picture.
• Task- and goal-oriented and well organised; works independently or as part of a larger team; comfortable in a high-paced, hands-on hardware environment.
• Communicates clearly in writing and in person; adaptable across several projects with shifting priorities and deadlines.
• Open-minded and confident to push back on design changes and tasks when the evidence says so.
• A problem-solver and fixer: not afraid to break things, cut to the cause and debug quickly.
• Brings energy, mentors others and helps grow the team.
What we offer
• A well-equipped personal bench, all the test equipment and software you need.
• A lab and instrument set-up that is being built now — you will help shape it.
• Cross-discipline project teams; an electronics team of two engineers plus placement students; direct influence on the next-generation instruments.

The practice
Finance is one of the most demanding and valuable environments in which to apply modern technology. You will work with complex enterprise data, mission-critical processes and high-impact decisions, using AI, data and engineering to reshape how organisations plan, control performance and allocate resources. The opportunity goes beyond building technically strong solutions: you will see how those solutions influence cash, profitability, risk and business growth, and take them from experimentation into trusted, production-ready capabilities. Working in Finance Reinvention allows you to remain close to leading-edge technology while developing an understanding of the CFO agenda, gaining exposure to senior decision-makers and building the commercial judgement needed to solve enterprise-wide challenges. This combination of deep technical capability, finance-domain expertise and measurable business impact creates a differentiated career path that is difficult to develop in a purely technology-focused role.
Purpose of the role
Core build capability for the practice. Responsible for engineering agents, the orchestration around them, the evaluation harness that establishes whether they perform, and the finance user surfaces through which they are operated. The role designs, develops, tests, deploys and operates production-grade AI applications and the services around them. Embedded within a delivery pod and working on client data from an early stage of each engagement, the role translates finance-process and control requirements into secure, observable and maintainable software.
Responsibilities
• Build and deploy agentic workflows into live finance processes, including reconciliations, journals, exception handling, disputes, collections and variance explanation, with clear acceptance criteria, human oversight and controlled failure behaviour.
• Implement LLM application patterns including tool and function calling, structured outputs, RAG or graph-based retrieval, context and memory management, multi-agent orchestration, and prompt or configuration versioning.
• Integrate with ERP and EPM systems, document repositories and workflow tooling, including the data extraction, transformation and error handling that integration requires, using secure APIs, events, identity controls and reusable connectors where appropriate.
• Write evaluations, instrument agent behaviour, and ensure failure modes are visible and recoverable, using automated functional and non-functional tests, trace-level observability, red-team scenarios and measures for quality, groundedness, latency and cost.
• Build the interfaces through which finance users review, approve, override and evidence agent actions, including provenance, citations, feedback capture, accessibility and clear error-recovery journeys.

Utility Infrastructure –

Social Infrastructure -
Our team of Social Infrastructure specialists revitalise homes and communities by carrying out a wide range of work, from retrofit to refurbishment, and maintenance.

If there is anything we can do to support you, remove barriers, or make the process more accessible, please let us know — we want this to be the best possible experience for you.
Role Overview
UIPTD is seeking a Principal Structural Engineer to lead structural design and technical governance across our overhead line and substation structures portfolio, supporting EPC delivery for SSE, SPEN, NGED, and National Grid. The successful candidate will work closely alongside the incumbent team during a structured handover period to absorb corporate knowledge and technical authority. OHL structural experience (lattice towers, wood pole lines, or similar guyed/self-supporting structures) is strongly desired given how specialised this discipline is, but UIPTD will also consider candidates from adjacent structural disciplines — steel lattice/mast structures, telecoms towers, bridges, or other slender/dynamically-loaded structures — where the underlying engineering principles and analytical approach transfer well to OHL. Full training and mentoring into OHL-specific practice will be provided where required.
Key Responsibilities
Technical Leadership & Governance
•
Act as the senior structural design authority for OHL lattice tower, wood pole, and steel pole structures across UIPTD's EPC portfolio
•
Provide structural design authority for substation equipment support structures — gantries, busbar supports, plant support steelwork, cable sealing end structures
•
Lead complex or non-standard structural assessments, including heritage/legacy tower types, uprating studies, and load reassessment for line refurbishment or reconductoring schemes
•
Review and approve structural calculations and reports produced by senior and intermediate engineers within the team
•
Set and maintain UIPTD's structural design standards, procedures, and calculation templates for OHL and substation structures
•
Provide technical sign-off on structural elements of tender and PQQ submissions for OHL and substation framework contracts
•
Represent UIPTD at client technical governance meetings on structural matters (SSE, SPEN, NGED, National Grid)
OHL Structural Design
•
Structural analysis and design of lattice towers, wood pole (single, H-pole, trident) and steel pole structures
•
Tower/pole capacity studies for reconductoring, uprating, and line diversion schemes — assessing existing structures against revised loading
•
Review of PLS-CADD / PLS-POLE structural outputs and integration with the wider OHL design process
•
Structural input to feasibility studies and options assessments for new-build and refurbishment OHL schemes
Substation Structures
•
Structural design of substation gantries, busbar support structures, plant support steelwork, and cable sealing end structures
•
Structural assessment of existing substation structures for plant replacement or uprating schemes
•
Coordination with electrical and civil disciplines on substation structural interfaces
Mentoring, Succession & Team Development
•
Work directly alongside incumbent senior structural engineers during a structured handover period, to capture corporate knowledge, historic design precedent, and client-specific practice
•
Mentor and technically supervise Senior and Intermediate Structural Engineers within the team
•
Support recruitment, onboarding, and development of the wider structural engineering function
•
Champion structural engineering competency development across the OHL and substation design team
Quality, Safety & CDM
•
Ensure all structural design outputs comply with technical specifications, and client-specific standards
•
Author and review Designers Risk Assessments and structural design intent documentation under CDM 2015
•
Contribute to Temporary Works design and checking where structural expertise is required (tower propping, guying, temporary support systems)
•
Champion safe-by-design principles across all structural outputs
Requirements
Essential
•
Degree in Structural, Civil, or Mechanical Engineering (or equivalent); Chartered Engineer (CEng) with IStructE, ICE, or equivalent professional body
•
Minimum 10 years structural engineering experience, with demonstrable experience of slender, guyed, or dynamically-loaded structures (lattice towers, masts, poles, or similar)
•
Strong working knowledge of structural steel design and structural analysis principles applicable to lattice and pole structures
•
Experience of foundation design principles for structures subject to overturning, uplift, and lateral loading
•
Demonstrated ability to lead technically complex structural assessments and provide design authority sign-off
•
Strong mentoring and team leadership capability, with experience developing less experienced engineers
•
Full UK driving licence
Desirable
•
Direct experience of OHL lattice tower, wood pole, or steel pole structural design
•
Experience of PLS-CADD / PLS-POLE or equivalent OHL structural analysis software
•
Experience of substation structural design (gantries, plant support steelwork)
•
Experience of structural design in adjacent disciplines — telecoms masts, transmission towers, bridges, or other wind/dynamically-sensitive structures — where transferable to OHL
•
Experience of tower/pole capacity assessment for reconductoring or uprating schemes
•
Experience of SSE, SPEN, NGED, or National Grid framework delivery
•
CDM 2015 Principal Designer or Designer experience
What UIPTD Offers
•
Senior-level salary package commensurate with experience
•
Hybrid working arrangement — Horsham preferred, Glasgow or Warrington considered
•
A genuinely succession-critical role with direct handover from long-standing incumbent technical authorities
•
Structured mentoring into OHL-specific structural practice for candidates from adjacent disciplines
•
Chartership support and CPD funding
•
Company pension scheme
•
25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
Join us at United Infrastructure and be part of our mission to deliver innovative and sustainable solutions to the complex infrastructure needs of the UK.

• Contribute to bids, pursuits, and practice-building activities including thought leadership and go-to-market initiatives

• Understanding of AI/ML applications in security — threat detection, behavioural analytics, anomaly detection, and predictive risk modelling
• Knowledge of securing AI systems — including AI pipelines, MLOps practices, data platform security, model registries, and inference endpoints
• Experience with AI-specific threats and controls: adversarial robustness, data integrity, model theft, and supply chain security
• Solid grounding in Identity and Access Management, including PAM, IGA, ITDR, and machine/non-human identity governance

Key focus: Positioning Accenture as the partner of choice for clients looking to harness AI for security and build trustworthy, secure AI at scale — with identity as a critical control plane across both.

Evolito’s mission is to accelerate the adoption of electric propulsion in aerospace applications in support of a net-zero world.  We will help to revolutionise personal mobility and transform our towns and cities with clean, noise-free air transportation.
Evolito develops and manufactures class-leading, lightweight, high-power, and high-torque-density electric propulsion systems for a range of aerospace markets, including EVTOL, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles and General Aviation.
As well as ultra-high performance, low-weight electric motors and controllers, Evolito specialises in high integrity, bespoke battery systems for the aerospace and defence markets. The team is scaling rapidly and has ambitious growth plans over the next twelve to eighteen months.
As part of our current high-growth phase, we are creating our Research and Technology (R&T) team and are looking for a Senior Technical Specialist – Thermal Engineer to join us.
The R&T team is responsible for the development of new systems, electric machines and power control electronics in support of new and existing customers. This includes electric propulsion systems, electrical generation systems and power management systems for all-electric and hybrid-electric aircraft.
As the Senior Technical Specialist – Thermal Engineer, you will deliver the design of thermal systems for new product, including motors, electronic units and whole electric propulsion units (EPU), based on the combined evaluation of thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer. In addition, you will be responsible for the design and development of new concepts to optimise EPU performance and durability that are suitable for manufacture, as well as specify and guide physical testing required to verify CAE analyses and provide data to support conclusions.
Key responsibilities will include:
•
Owning the design of thermal systems for Evolito's product range
•
Validate and assess results against real-world constraints and draw sound conclusions
•
Guide Designers and Systems Engineers during the design phase for optimised solutions based on thermal and pressure drop results
•
Analysis of complete/sealed liquid cooling systems including major loss contributors and heat dissipators
•
Specification of pumps for coolant flows and required airflow to support liquid/air heat exchangers
•
Specification of heat exchangers based on cooling requirements and fluid flow rates
•
Liaise with key suppliers and customers on design and development issues, resolve to the optimal solution and understand the compromises
•
Understand design for assembly and constraints for high volume manufacture
•
Write specifications and reports as required through the product lifecycle, utilising a structured approach to problem-solving techniques.
Skills and experience required:
•
Degree or equivalent in a degree related to thermal engineering
•
Strong mechanical or electrical engineering background, but more importantly, be able to apply knowledge to real-world situations
•
Practical knowledge in the design, use, and application of electric machines or rotational/complex components
•
Experience with finite element analysis methods e.g. CFD and programs e.g. ANSYS Fluent
•
Self-sufficient and able to work with minimal managerial input
•
Confident with customers and suppliers, able to detail requirements and understand issues
•
Strong communication skills (both written and verbal), good collaboration skills, and the ability to work effectively across teams
•
Results-orientated, and able to deliver business value
•
Self-motivated with the determination to succeed
•
A flexible approach to work with the desire to thrive in a dynamic, fast-moving environment
•
Willingness to travel as required.
Desirable:
•
Familiarity with programming e.g. Python, or using programmes in LabView or MATLAB

Our team leaders are fulfilled by the idea of affecting even the smallest positive changes in our young people, so we celebrate the little things.

Compassionate, emotionally resilient, and supportive, you’ll also be able to provide the leadership that inspires your colleagues.
What we do for you

• Progression: If career development is your thing, most of our team leaders and managers have been promoted from within our group – plus you could join our ‘Aspire’ future managers programme
• Flexible benefits package: meaning you can increase/decrease your holiday allowance, pension and life insurance – check out our benefits here
• Wellbeing: a host of wellbeing tools and advice including employee assistance
• Medical cover so you can claim back the cost of things like an opticians or dentist appointment and a host of high-street discounts
• Meals provided while you’re at work
• Beautiful working environments with the very best facilities – check out our homes here
• A recommend a friend scheme that offers a £1,000 bonus every time
Bring your whole-self to work
Here at Witherslack Group, we celebrate everyone’s differences as that’s what makes us the best at what we do. Our young people come from all walks of life, diverse backgrounds and with different needs – and our workforce reflects that diversity, so that our teams can engage, encourage and inspire our young people to be themselves. You don’t need experience, but there are a few things we’ll be looking for from you:
• A ‘can do’ attitude – a team player who rolls up their sleeves to help others
• We genuinely care about our young people (and each other) so honesty and empathy is a must
• The resilience to be able to deal with challenging situations
• A full UK driving licence which you’ve held for at least 12 months
• This role requires you to have the Level 3 Children’s Residential Care qualification
You’ll start life as a Team Leader by joining our ‘Care Academy’ – 4 weeks of off the job training with experienced WG professionals to help you feel confident and ready to support our young people.
Join the UK’s best special education and care provider
At Witherslack Group, inclusion is part of who we are. We’re committed to creating an environment where everyone feels respected, valued and that they truly belong.
As a specialist provider of education and care for children and young people with special educational needs, we understand the importance of embracing individuality and championing difference- especially when it comes to neurodiversity. We celebrate diverse perspectives, lived experiences, and the unique strengths that each person brings to our community.
We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities, and abilities. We are proud to be recognised as an inclusive employer and are committed to making our recruitment and workplace practices inclusive and accessible. If you need any adjustments to support you through the recruitment process or in the workplace, we’ll be there every step of the way.
By building a diverse and inclusive team, we’re better able to support the children, young people and families we serve and ensure every member of our team can thrive, grow, and be their authentic self.

At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.
Job Description
What if your next role could change someone's life?
Not in a vague, corporate-speak kind of way. We mean genuinely, concretely, and measurably change the life of a patient who is waiting for a treatment that does not yet exist.
At Bristol Myers Squibb, that is not an aspiration, it is our work. And we are looking for someone like you to help make it happen.
This is your invitation to shape medicines from day one
As a Senior Manager, Early Clinical Development, Clinical Pharmacology Studies, you will be embedded in the heart of early clinical development focused in clinical pharmacology. You will not be watching from the sidelines - you will be designing and providing clinical oversight for the clinical studies that move promising compounds from concept into patients' hands.
From drafting protocols and informed consent documents, reviewing clinical data for emerging trends, and authoring and/or reviewing clinical study reports, your fingerprints will be on every critical milestone of a clinical study. That is not a small thing - that is science with stakes.
What your day-to-day actually looks like
You will collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the field - cross-functional teams consisting of internal and external stakeholders - to bring rigour and clarity to complex, fast-moving, early development clinical pharmacology studies.
Concretely, you'll be:
• Crafting the blueprint – Developing and refining protocols and ICF documents, presenting them to governance committees, and ensuring every detail supports the science
• Protecting data integrity – Collaborating with data management to design data-focused eCRFs and contribute to Data Review Plans that are effective
• Telling the scientific story – Authoring and reviewing clinical study reports and contributing to regulatory submissions (INDs, IBs, DSURs, etc) which open doors to health authorities
• Raising the bar on-site – Building training materials and presenting at site initiation visits and investigator meetings so study sites are equipped to deliver high-quality data and proper care for study participants
• Keeping a finger on the pulse – Ongoing monitoring/review for clinical trends to ensure the safety of our study participants
What you will gain beyond the job title
• Depth of scientific impact - You will work across the lifecycle of early development clinical pharmacology studies (from phase 1 through phase 2a). The breadth will accelerate your development in ways that siloed roles simply cannot match.
• A global stage - Partnering internationally with KOLs, regulatory bodies, and cross-functional teams means your work and your network has no borders
• A clear growth trajectory - Reporting to the Executive Director of Clinical Science, you will have both the support of experienced leadership and the autonomy to build your capabilities
• The frontier of clinical pharmacology in early drug development - You will be working in the dynamic early development therapeutic areas of immunology, cardiovascular, haematology, and oncology
• A culture that backs you - BMS is a place where collaboration is encouraged daily. It is how “things get done.”  You will be part of a team that challenges each other and champions each other in equal measure.
You will thrive here if you…
• Hold a degree in Life Sciences (MD, PhD, PharmD, MS, RN, or equivalent) and bring 2+ years of experience in early drug development focused in clinical pharmacology
• Author/review clinical contributions to clinical study reports and clinical portions of regulatory documents (e.g., Pre-IND, IND, IB, DSUR, PSUR, Orphan Annual Reports, HA, EC, IRB responses and contributions to regulatory submissions)
• Proficient knowledge of GCP/ICH, early drug development clinical pharmacology, study designs, statistics, clinical operations, etc.
• Can identify things others miss and you care about getting it right
• Are comfortable navigating ambiguity - shifting priorities do not throw you, they energise you
• Bring solid medical writing skills and translate complex science into clear, compelling documents
Have intermediate skills in Microsoft Word/Excel/PowerPoint and data review tools (eg, patient profiles/narratives, report generating tools, etc)
Why BMS? Why now?
BMS has a bold ambition: to transform patients' lives through science. In this department it means being on the forefront of early drug development clinical pharmacology studies in support of tackling diseases that rob people of their quality of life.
BMS is at a pivotal moment in its early drug development clinical pharmacology pipeline, and the clinical scientists we bring on board today help define what is possible tomorrow.
A truly global role with approximately 10 – 20% domestic and international travel required
